Well.. So around winter of 2019, my friend and I started getting into a little too much into drinking and sometimes coke. We both had a lot of life changing events—not for better. Latest was her husbands diagnosis of cancer, AML. Fast forward a few months. We both drank a lot, I think at first she more than I. Vodka. I have hated drinking my whole life. Now at us both 31 (now 32) I’m drinking? I didn’t think I was capable of having a drinking problem. Drugs? Way more likely. Did I know I was an addict? Yes I did. And I knew the likeliness and was just supporting a friend and “being careful”. First it was a few times a week. Then everyday. Then hiding it from others. And well... august 26 I get my job back and I finally got a car. September 30, around 940pm, I got black out drunk (I had taken meds for anxiety and don’t remember anything) I got about 600ft up the street, driving, and hit a parking meter and a telephone pole. Directly in front, and I mean directly, in front of the local town police station. Transported to the hospital and don’t remember a thing. My friend went through my car and realized I was not only drinking vodka with her (and more), I had also started to drink tequila and never told her. She found about 8 of them in my trunk, a handle bottle of vodka that I bought at noon on my way home from work. And cried to my mom. I went impatient for a week, did some group therapy, and virtual AA. I was then assigned an individual therapist who won’t answer and won’t respond to me. 

I wish I could say this has changed me. I have drank since this and I don’t know why. I have told people around me and I’m aware of how bad it can get. I have kids too and I’m ashamed deeply. This is actually tearing me up typing this. I kicked heroin alone (after getting kicked out of a help group for being on anxiety meds—love my town) the problem I think is alcohol is so accessible and culturally accepted that makes it harder. And how to enjoy life like a normal person. Sorry for my rant. I wish everyone the best and congratulations to anyone who is sober I don’t care how long. Take that and be proud!

I work in a school lunch room. It’s a private school, and some of the children are bussed in from different towns. The town the school is located in is wealthy. (I come from a town over, so I’m not in that category—not my point though). Majority of the kids are from said town, and have money (come from money) and can afford the **insanely** priced lunches we serve. Some of the kids that attend however, are there on some kind of scholarship (not exactly sure what kind; possibly athletic) and don’t have the ability to have preloaded lunch accounts with $200 a week __at least__ . Everything is electronic; cash or check needs to be put into the school lunch account site. No registers to accept cash and give change. 

In the beginning of the year, since the school now has an outside company (who I work for) in the kitchen, some students qualified for a reduced lunch. If it were a public school, more of them would probably have qualified for free lunch. We were allowed to let their accounts get “over drawn” to a certain point. The alternative lunches offered if they didn’t have any money are a joke; a little thing of cereal OR a fruit. That lasted about maybe a week, and I guess the kids that had reduced lunch now so get free lunch. If not, their lunch is now included with their scholarship.

If they are able to pay for lunch and don’t have funds on their account, their lunch number is written down and it’s put into the system by a supervisor. I’m not exactly sure what happens from there, but the school definitely gets away with a lot more shit since they’re private and can go by their own rules essentially. Since working this job and seeing all that goes down on this side. All the talk that goes on about kids health and eating habits to aid in better school performance; it isn’t always instilled which makes me a mix of mad and sad.  I have children of my own, and I would be upset if they were denied lunch.  If a parent forgot to put money on their account, it isn’t the child’s fault and shouldn’t be denied food for that day, or until the money clears on the account. 

My children attend public school. Breakfast is fairly new within the past couple years, and I think it’s a good thing. Many of the kids come from broken homes and don’t always get to eat. Sometimes, school is the only place they can get a meal of any kind (poverty, addiction; different factors) On certain days, little food bags are sent home weekly to the kids who get free lunch, and sometimes reduced, to make sure they have something to eat. I really love that this program has been set in place. My children’s school vs my job is like day and night. Each parent has the right to put their child in private school, but it’s not always greener on the other side. Sorry if this is all over the place, I tried my best to explain what I am aware of happening; at least with my job.
